h1: Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai — 5-Star Luxury with Skybridge BTS Access, the Best-Positioned Hotel Near Ramathibodi Hospital
intro: Picture stepping out of the lobby and walking — without touching a street or standing in the sun — directly onto the BTS Skytrain or Airport Rail Link that will take you to Suvarnabhumi Airport in 45 minutes. Then returning to the 37th-floor infinity pool as Bangkok's skyline blazes gold at dusk. Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai is a five-star hotel that opened in 2023 inside The Unicorn Building on Phaya Thai Road, Ratchathewi. Two things make it stand out above everything else in this part of the city: a direct indoor skybridge to both BTS Phaya Thai and Airport Rail Link Phaya Thai stations, and a location just ~1.2 km (~6 min by car / ~15 min on foot) from Ramathibodi Hospital on Rama VI Road. That combination makes it the go-to choice for patients' families, medical visitors, and anyone who wants genuine luxury within easy reach of one of Bangkok's busiest teaching hospitals. 494 rooms. From approx. ฿4,500/night. Score 9.6 from 4,855 verified guest reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Who is Eastin Grand Phayathai best for? — In plain terms, this hotel serves two audiences exceptionally well. First, patients and families visiting Ramathibodi Hospital: people who need a clean, quiet, safe base with reliable transport to the hospital, without the stress of a chaotic environment. Second, business travellers and tourists who want genuine five-star polish in a part of Bangkok that connects to the airport and the city's rail network faster than almost any other address. The hotel opened in 2023 in The Unicorn Building on Phaya Thai Road — a location whose key engineering trick is a covered skybridge linking the hotel directly to BTS Phaya Thai Station (N2) and Airport Rail Link Phaya Thai Station (A8) without a single step outdoors. With a score of 9.6 from 4,855 Trip.com reviews and 9.5 from over 6,000 Booking.com reviews, the numbers confirm that most guests leave satisfied. Reviewers consistently describe it as the right choice for anyone who values newness, cleanliness, and frictionless transit connections in their Bangkok stay.

Location and transport — including distance to Ramathibodi Hospital — The hotel sits at 18 Phaya Thai Road, Thung Phaya Thai, Ratchathewi, inside The Unicorn Building. Its most valuable practical asset is the indoor skybridge that connects directly to BTS Phaya Thai and Airport Rail Link Phaya Thai — meaning you can reach both train systems in air-conditioned comfort, rain or shine. For visitors to Ramathibodi Hospital (270 Rama VI Road, Ratchathewi, Mahidol University): the hotel is approximately 1.2 km away — roughly 6 minutes by Grab or taxi in normal traffic, or about 15 minutes on foot via Phaya Thai Road and Rama VI Road. Families making daily hospital runs will find this distance very manageable. The neighbourhood also has 7-Elevens, pharmacies, and restaurants within a few minutes, and the broader Ratchathewi area around Victory Monument is alive with street food and local services. For leisure: three to four BTS stops takes you to Siam Paragon, Central World, and the Pratunam shopping district, while Airport Rail Link delivers you to Suvarnabhumi Airport in approximately 45 minutes.

"We stayed here while my father was being treated at Ramathibodi. The Grab ride to the hospital was under 10 minutes every morning. The room was immaculate and the bed was the most comfortable thing I've slept in during a very difficult week. Genuinely grateful this hotel exists."

Room types and interiors — The 494 rooms and suites in The Unicorn Building span several tiers across 34–370 sqm. The Superior Room (34 sqm) comes in King or Twin configuration, fits two adults and one child under 16, and is the starting point. Superior Panorama (34 sqm) adds a more prominent city view angle. The mid-tier Deluxe with Lounge Access (46–50 sqm) is a corner room with panoramic city views, an in-room espresso machine, and access to the Executive Lounge. Above that sit One-Bedroom Suite, Premium One-Bedroom Suite, Two-Bedroom Suite, and the Penthouse Suite at 370 sqm. The aesthetic is contemporary luxury — neutral tones, high ceilings, artful lighting, and floor-to-ceiling windows framing the skyline. Real guest reviews consistently praise the newness and cleanliness of rooms, quality bedding, strong shower pressure, and thoughtful bathroom amenities. Two caveats worth flagging honestly: Superior rooms may not include an in-room coffee machine, which surprises some guests at a five-star property; and a few reviewers mention that light seeping around blackout curtains can make rooms less than completely dark. Both are easily resolved by requesting Deluxe or above when booking, and by asking for extra curtain coverage if needed.

Facilities: pools, spa, and gym — The headline amenity is the pair of outdoor infinity pools on floors 22 and 37, both with sweeping Bangkok skyline views. Multiple reviews describe the views as genuinely spectacular — the kind that prompts guests to photograph them from every angle. The evening light is universally cited as the best time to use the pools. Honest note: reviewers mention the rooftop pools can be windy and the water cooler than expected, especially from November onward, and reaching the upper pool requires changing lifts mid-journey due to the building's elevator zoning. Bhu Mhai Spa on the 38th floor is a full-service wellness centre with individually tailored treatment programmes, and consistently earns high marks from guests who used it — particularly relevant for families carrying stress from hospital visits who want a proper decompression session. The 24-hour fitness centre is well-equipped with cardio machines, free weights, and resistance equipment. The hotel also provides free parking, EV charging points, a business centre, multiple meeting rooms, and a grand ballroom.

Dining and service — Trattoria@22 serves Mediterranean and international cuisine on floor 22 with city views. The Market@5 is an all-day dining venue in a market-style format that handles breakfast — reviews note it runs until 11:00 AM, which is welcome for guests on a flexible hospital schedule. Breakfast variety earns consistent praise. A ground-floor café handles lighter bites and drinks. On service, the majority of reviews use words like "friendly," "professional," and "genuinely helpful." The hotel uses a QR-code messaging system that reduces language barriers — a practical touch that matters for international families at Ramathibodi. Staff have been praised for handling special requests such as birthday setups and packed takeaway breakfasts. Honest notes: some reviewers feel the breakfast quality doesn't fully match five-star expectations, and coffee comes from an automatic machine rather than a handcrafted espresso setup. The Executive Lounge runs 17:00–19:30 only, which conflicts directly with dinner hours, meaning guests who book Lounge Access rooms may struggle to benefit from that perk.

Real guest feedback — the full picture — Aggregated from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the pattern is clear. What guests consistently love: the skybridge transit connection that eliminates outdoor walking in Bangkok heat; the freshness and cleanliness of rooms in a hotel barely two years old; the two-pool rooftop experience with the Bangkok skyline; friendly, attentive staff; the 24-hour gym; and free parking for self-drive visitors. What guests flag as weaknesses: elevator waits during peak hours in a 494-room property can stretch long — a real issue if you need to leave for a hospital appointment at a fixed time. Some Superior rooms lack in-room coffee makers. One reviewer reported an unannounced room entry while at breakfast, which is a rare but legitimate concern worth noting (hang the Do Not Disturb sign when you leave). The rooftop pools can be windier and cooler than expected. None of these are dealbreakers — the overall score of 9.6 tells its own story — but they are real, and worth knowing.

"The room was spotless, the view from the 37th-floor pool was genuinely jaw-dropping, and the staff handled every request without hesitation. Only gripe: the lifts during morning rush are slow. Build in extra time if you have a hospital appointment."

Pricing and value — Superior rooms start from approximately ฿4,500–5,000/night (around US$130–140) in the low-to-mid season. Deluxe Lounge Access rooms begin around ฿6,500, and suite categories run from ฿9,500 upwards into the five-figure range during peak season. For a brand-new five-star hotel with a skybridge to both the city rail and airport rail systems, two rooftop pools, a dedicated spa floor, and a score north of 9.5 on multiple major platforms, the pricing represents genuine value within the Bangkok five-star bracket. For families accompanying a patient at Ramathibodi, the marginal cost over a mid-range option may well be worth it: the environment is calming, the beds are hotel-quality, the transport is seamless, and the spa offers real stress relief. High season runs November through February — book well ahead and compare Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com for the best rate.

Before you book: practical notes — A few tips that will make your stay run more smoothly. One: allow 10–15 extra minutes when leaving for Ramathibodi Hospital during morning rush hours — the lifts on a busy morning in a large property can add unexpected delay. Two: if having a coffee machine in the room matters to you, book Deluxe Lounge Access or above — Superior rooms may not include one, and the listing does not always make this clear. Three: the hotel has free parking and EV charging, which is a genuine advantage if you are driving yourself or renting a car for hospital logistics. Four: use the Airport Rail Link connection for both arriving from and departing to Suvarnabhumi — it is genuinely one of the most seamless airport-to-room transitions in Bangkok. Five: the surrounding Ratchathewi district is a business and transit hub rather than a food-market neighbourhood; for street food and local colour, a two-stop BTS ride to Victory Monument or Pratunam opens up a different world.

honestSummary: Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai delivers on its promise: a genuinely new, clean, and well-staffed five-star hotel with a skybridge to both Bangkok rail systems and a short cab ride to Ramathibodi Hospital. The two rooftop pools and Bhu Mhai Spa elevate it beyond just a transit-convenient property. The honest caveats are real — elevator waits during peak hours, some Superior rooms without coffee machines, and an Executive Lounge whose narrow window makes it hard to use — but none of them undercut the 9.6 score that thousands of guests have given it.

tips.body: The rooftop infinity pool on floor 37 is most impressive around 17:00–18:30 before the wind picks up. Worth timing your swim to catch the city lights coming on.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai Bangkok

faq.q: How far is Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai from Ramathibodi Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is located at 18 Phaya Thai Road, Ratchathewi, approximately 1.2 km from Ramathibodi Hospital (270 Rama VI Road, Ratchathewi, Mahidol University). That works out to roughly 6 minutes by Grab or taxi in normal traffic, or about 15 minutes on foot along Phaya Thai Road and Rama VI Road. For families making daily hospital visits, this is a very convenient and low-stress distance.

faq.q: Does Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai have direct access to the BTS and Airport Rail Link?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has an indoor covered skybridge that connects directly to BTS Phaya Thai Station (N2) and Airport Rail Link Phaya Thai Station (A8) without any outdoor walking. This means you can reach both rail systems in air-conditioned comfort regardless of weather. The Airport Rail Link takes approximately 45 minutes to Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK). BTS connects to Siam, Chitlom, and the rest of the Sukhumvit and Silom lines.

faq.q: What are the room types and starting prices at Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai?
faq.a: Rooms range from 34 sqm Superior Rooms from approx. ฿4,500/night (around US$130) in the standard season, up to Penthouse Suites at 370 sqm. Mid-tier Deluxe Lounge Access rooms (46–50 sqm, corner position, espresso machine, Executive Lounge included) start around ฿6,500. One-Bedroom Suites begin around ฿9,500. Prices in high season (November–February) increase noticeably — compare Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com for the best current rate.

faq.q: How many pools does Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai have, and where are they?
faq.a: The hotel has two outdoor infinity pools — on floors 22 and 37 — both with panoramic Bangkok skyline views. The 37th-floor pool offers the wider view and is the more iconic of the two. Honest note: both pools can be windy and cooler than expected, particularly from November through February, and reaching the upper pool requires switching lifts. Bhu Mhai Spa is on floor 38, directly above the top pool.

faq.q: Is Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai suitable for families accompanying a patient at Ramathibodi Hospital?
faq.a: Very much so. The hotel's combination of a short, predictable ride to Ramathibodi (~6 min by Grab), immaculate new rooms, quality beds, and a calm five-star environment makes it genuinely supportive during a stressful medical stay. Free parking accommodates families driving themselves, and the spa and pools offer real decompression. The one practical note: allow extra time for lifts during the morning peak if you have a fixed appointment. Book Deluxe or above to get an in-room coffee machine.

faq.q: When did Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai open, and how many rooms does it have?
faq.a: The hotel opened in 2023 inside The Unicorn Building at 18 Phaya Thai Road, Ratchathewi, Bangkok. It has 494 rooms and suites across multiple categories, from 34 sqm Superior Rooms to a 370 sqm Penthouse Suite, spanning floors in the high-rise Unicorn Building that also houses a shopping complex, restaurants, pharmacy, and convenience stores at its base.
